title: Command guard rules (shared/policies/command-guard.json)
description: Rules that map command patterns to deny, require_grant:<activity> or allow (§12.3). Every matcher in a rule's match must hold for the rule to apply. Any deny wins (the first deny rule in file order is reported), then require_grant (activities accumulate), then allow. The guard module also checks what this schema cannot: unique rule IDs, the activity named by require_grant, and that every regex compiles.

effect.description: deny, allow, or require_grant:<activity> with an activity from defs.schema.json.

reason.description: Why the rule exists; the decision's reason starts with it.

program.description: Glob patterns (fnmatch) for the program's lower-cased base name, after wrappers are stripped.

unless_program.description: There is a program, and it is not one of these globs given as a bare name found on the PATH.

declared_activity.description: The command declares one of these activities.

subcommand.description: The first argument that is not an option is one of these. The values of git's global options that take one (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --super-prefix, --config-env, --attr-source) are skipped. Arguments after the subcommand become the arguments the args_* matchers see.

unless_subcommand.description: There is a subcommand and it is none of these.

args_all.description: Every one of these is an argument (exact match).

args_any.description: At least one of these is an argument (exact match).

unless_args.description: None of these is an argument (exact match).

no_args.description: The program has no arguments after it, once wrappers are stripped. true is the only value.

args_regex.description: Some argument matches this Python regex (re.search).

args_regex_on_stdin.description: args_regex also reads what the program is fed on stdin: the arguments of the commands before it in its pipe, and here-string and here-document bodies. true is the only value.

shell_regex.description: The command comes from a shell string that matches this Python regex (re.search) as a whole.

check.description: A named check implemented by the guard module.
